title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: KENDRA'S BOAT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Kendra Mills, a shrimp boat deckhand from Biloxi, Mississippi.
She can haul a net in a thunderstorm. But her little sister's posts sank her every time.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SCROLL
segments.quote: Do not spoil what you have by desiring what you have not.
segments.author: Epicurus
lines: Monique does the weather on TV in Atlanta. Big hair, big smile, big following.
At four in the morning, Kendra scrolled on the dock and felt two inches tall.
Captain Earl tapped a page from Epicurus, a Greek thinker:
Do not spoil what you have by desiring what you have not.
Kendra looked up. Ten years ago, this sunrise was all she wanted.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BLAZER
segments.quote: Most people are other people. Their thoughts are some one else's opinions, their lives a mimicry, their passions a quotation.
segments.author: Oscar Wilde
lines: Mama's sixtieth birthday party was coming. So Kendra bought a blazer and practiced saying synergy.
Earl read her a line from Oscar Wilde:
Most people are other people. Their thoughts are some one else's opinions, their lives a mimicry, their passions a quotation.
She returned the blazer and bought new white shrimp boots.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: SATURDAYS
segments.quote: Small opportunities are often the beginning of great enterprises.
segments.author: Demosthenes
lines: Kendra dreamed of running her own sunset fishing trips.
Earl offered his old boat, the Miss Lula, on Saturdays. Six seats. Smelled like bait.
Too small, she thought. Earl quoted Demosthenes, the Greek speaker:
Small opportunities are often the beginning of great enterprises.
She said yes. Her first two guests got seasick, and still left five stars.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE LICENSE
segments.quote: He that would have the fruit must climb the tree.
segments.author: Thomas Fuller
lines: To do it for real, she needed a captain's license. The study book weighed more than a bag of shrimp.
Mama texted her a saying from Thomas Fuller, an English doctor:
He that would have the fruit must climb the tree.
So she climbed. Flash cards on the ice chest. Knots at red lights. Three months later, she passed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: DEAD ENGINE
segments.quote: Do what you can, with what you have, where you are.
segments.author: Theodore Roosevelt
lines: Her first full Saturday, the engine died two miles out.
Six people stared. Her hands shook. Then she remembered Theodore Roosevelt:
Do what you can, with what you have, where you are.
She dropped anchor, lit the camp stove, and made a shrimp boil right there. The guests booked again.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: SISTERS
segments.quote: Grief can take care of itself; but to get the full value of a joy you must have somebody to divide it with.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: At Mama's party, Monique whispered, I watch your sunrise videos every morning. I'm jealous.
All those years, they'd been envying each other. Mama raised a glass to Mark Twain:
Grief can take care of itself; but to get the full value of a joy you must have somebody to divide it with.
Next morning, the sisters rode the Miss Lula at sunrise. Monique got seasick. Kendra held her hair.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Love what you have. Be yourself. Take the small chance. Climb. Use what's in reach. Share the joy.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Love what you have. Be yourself. Take the small chance. Climb. Use what's in reach. Share the joy.
Me? I get seasick in the bathtub.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
